english: Let $S$ be the set of all complex numbers $z$ satisfying $|z-8|=3|z|$. Let $M$ and $m$ be the maximum and the minimum values of $|z-14-8i|$ over $z\in S$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Then the value of $M^{2}+m^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $z$ का समुच्चय है जो $|z-8|=3|z|$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं। माना कि $z\in S$ पर $|z-14-8i|$ के अधिकतम तथा न्यूनतम मान क्रमशः $M$ तथा $m$ हैं, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। तब $M^{2}+m^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $|z-8|^{2}=9|z|^{2}$: $(x-8)^{2}+y^{2}=9(x^{2}+y^{2})\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+2x-8=0$, the Apollonius circle with centre $-1$, radius $3$
$p=14+8i$: distance from the centre $=|15+8i|=17>3$, so $p$ is outside
Triangle inequality: $17-3\leq|z-p|\leq17+3$, both attained on the line through the centre and $p$: $m=14$, $M=20$
solution_full: So $S$ is the circle $(x+1)^{2}+y^{2}=9$: centre $c=-1$, radius $3$. (Check: $z=2$ gives $6=3\cdot2$; $z=-4$ gives $12=3\cdot4$.)
Equality holds at the two points where the line through $c$ and $p$ meets the circle, so $M=20$ and $m=14$.
originality_note: New: the Apollonius circle is used only as the carrier of a distance extremum, with the point placed so that the answer comes through the triangle inequality (way 5). Closest known: maximum and minimum of |z - p| on a circle; Apollonius circle |z - a| = k|z - b|. Different because: the circle must first be recovered from the ratio form before the extremum; this is a routine combination, flagged as standard ingredients.

concept_use.Triangle Inequalities & Modulus Extremum: | |c-p| - r | <= |z-p| <= |c-p| + r gives m = 14 and M = 20.

key_step: Convert the ratio condition to the circle centre -1, radius 3, then max/min distance = 17 +- 3.
justification: Two standard steps chained (Apollonius circle, distance extremum); routine, no insight. Above 2025-P1-Q7 (L1) because of the extra extremum step, so level 2.
